name: BeagleBone Black P8 Header
summary: The GPIO side of the BeagleBone Black. Most of it is already spoken for by the on-board eMMC and HDMI, which is the first thing to work out before wiring a cape.
notes: Pins 27 to 46 drive the on-board HDMI framer. They are yours only after disabling HDMI in the device tree, and doing that costs you video output.
Pins 3 to 6 and 20 to 25 go to the on-board eMMC. Taking them means booting from microSD instead.
Between HDMI and eMMC, a stock board leaves roughly ten pins on P8 genuinely free. Plan the cape around that, not around the 46 holes.
Signal names here are the power-on defaults. Nearly every pin muxes to something else, and several reach the PRU, the real reason to pick this board over a Pi.
GPIO are 3.3 V and not 5 V tolerant, at 4 to 6 mA per pin.
The P8 and P9 headers are keyed the same and sit the same distance apart as on the original BeagleBone, so older capes still fit.
The other side of this board is the P9 header, documented separately: gwark.dev/openlabbench/pinouts/beaglebone-black-p9
